ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and senior managing officials against the following: (i) South African FICA list/Board notices; (ii) OFAC SDN list; (iii) EU Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (v) UK HM Treasury Consolidated List; and (vi) South Africa's domestic targeted financial sanctions list under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004. PEP identification must follow FATF and FICA definitions, covering domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs, including relatives and close associates. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for PEPs from high-risk third countries and for any private-banking or cross-border correspondent relationships. Ongoing monitoring and re-screening must occur at least every 90 days and upon any material change in ownership/control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Online Filing System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be in English, Afrikaans, or any recognized Latin-script language. All names must be transliterated into Latin characters for CIPC records. The name must not be grossly offensive, falsely imply connection with the government, or conflict with existing registered names or trademarks. The expression '(Pty) Ltd' (Proprietary Limited) is mandatory as a corporate appellation and appears in Latin script. Foreign-language names must include a full English transliteration and, if deemed necessary, a certified translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC name rejection, the applicant must, within 20 business days of the rejection notice, file an administrative appeal via the CIPC e-services portal or by email to the CIPC Compliance Unit. The appeal must attach: (i) a copy of the CIPC name-rejection letter; (ii) written legal argument demonstrating non-conflict or entitlement to the name; and (iii) proof of payment of the nominal appeal fee. In the alternative, the applicant may apply for reconsideration to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 30 business days. The applicant may also submit a revised name application immediately while preserving the original reservation date if the rejection is evidential. If the Companies Tribunal or CIPC again rejects the name, the applicant may file an application for judicial review with the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For the target high-frequency algorithmic trading entity, a virtual-only office is not sufficient. South African law (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s 23) requires a registered office that is a physical address in South Africa accessible to the public and to regulatory authorities, and not a post-office box. The chosen venue must have full-time staff, active business signage, and suitable infrastructure for trading operations and record-keeping. A co-working/serviced office or a professional law-firm address may be accepted if it provides physical presence and a responsible person to receive official documents; however, the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) will expect a genuine local operational hub for the licensed FSP. Therefore, only a dedicated physical office or a top-tier serviced office with independent meeting/records rooms should be used.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for regulated financial services: 45%–60% probability of an unannounced FSCA/Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) inspection within the first 18 months of operation. An on-site compliance review is considered standard for newly licensed market-making and proprietary trading firms. Even in the pre-incorporation phase, a desk-relevance assessment will be performed, and any inconsistency in the physical address will trigger immediate scrutiny.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, Chapter 4 (Incorporation of Companies); Regulations 2011, sections 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. The company may commence business immediately after incorporation, and issued share capital must be accurately disclosed in the first annual return.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY: 1. That the subscription of 100 ordinary shares at ZAR 1.00 each be accepted and issued to the founding subscribers. 2. That the registered office be established at the address stated in the Memorandum of Incorporation, and that the Company Secretary or a designated director be authorised to attend to all CIPC notifications. 3. That the Directors and Officers identified in the Incorporation Record be appointed with full authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and convene shareholder meetings. 4. That all further filing and licensing action be delegated to the appointed Officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve and Verify Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the CIPC portal, select 'Company Name Reservation' (Form CoR 9.1). Submit the proposed name, confirm compliance with the Companies Act naming provisions, and pay the reservation fee. The name reservation is valid for 20 business days; renew if necessary. Ensure the proposed name 'ZA PTY LTD' is not misleading or reserved for exclusive use.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or confusion, file a fresh name reservation with alternative names or submit a formal objection/request for reconsideration through the CIPC dispute resolution queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Memorandum of Incorporation and Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI in English, including the company's incorporation date, share classes, director provisions, registered office address, and business purpose covering proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading. Have the MOI and Form CoR 14.1 executed by each incorporator and, where required, have the documents notarized by a South African notary public.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form CoR 1.1) or equivalent
Identity and residential address proof of each director
Statement of issued shares and share premium
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Review the CIPC validation remarks; correct any missing annexures or MOI provisions identified in the provisional rejection notice and re-submit within the prescribed 30-day correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Documents with CIPC and Pay Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed MOI, CoR 14.1, and director consents to the CIPC corporate registration module. Pay the statutory filing fee using the designated payment gateway. Monitor the application status until CIPC issues the incorporation certificate (Form CoR 14.3) and unique company registration number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the query through the CIPC online portal, provide missing documentation or clarifications within 10 business days, and if rejected, file an appeal with CIPC or re-file a rectified submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold First Board Meeting and Adopt Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Pty Ltd
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting physically or by electronic communication. Adopt the pro-forma board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, officer appointments, and authorization to open bank accounts and engage the South African Revenue Service (SARS). Record minutes and maintain a statutory share register.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a directorship is disqualified under the Companies Act, reconvene the board to appoint a successor and file the amended CoR 1.1 with CIPC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with SARS, UIF, and Follow-on Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and relevant financial regulators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an income tax number, VAT registration (if applicable), and Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) / UIF registration for employees through SARS eFiling or the branch office. For the algorithmic high-frequency trading activity, submit the business description and confirm whether a Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) license or exemption applies under the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002 or the Financial Markets Act 19 of 2012.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS or FSCA queries the application, respond with a detailed business narrative clarifying the proprietary nature of the trading activity and any exemption from the requirement to hold a financial services provider license; appeal any adverse decision within the statutory timeline.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity comprises office-based algorithmic trading, not a listed EIA activity under Listing Notices 1 and 2 of the EIA Regulations, 2014; no physical manufacturing or waste discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – no industrial effluent, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the local Fire Protection Service following an inspection of the trading office; secure structural load approval from the municipal building control authority for server racks and specialized electronic equipment; register the premises with the Department of Employment and Labour for Compenser for Occupational Injuries and Diseases (COIDA) and display the compliance certificate in the workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — national tax and customs administration; online filing and registration portal: SARS eFiling at https://www.sars.gov.za and https://efiling.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned or locally incorporated (Pty) Ltd must first apply for an Income Tax reference number through SARS eFiling by submitting the relevant registration declaration (ITREG/IT application form) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation, a resolution appointing a Public Officer resident in South Africa under section 60 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, and proof of registered office address. Foreign-incorporated entities without local incorporation must further demonstrate a South African permanent establishment or appoint a representative taxpayer to obtain a tax reference number. For VAT purposes, a separate VAT vendor registration application (form VAT101) must be lodged on the same eFiling profile where taxable supplies exceed the compulsory turnover threshold or where voluntary registration criteria are satisfied; SARS may request a detailed business plan, financial projections, and third-party verification for high-risk or non-resident applicants.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a South African resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed as a separate legal taxpayer on its worldwide income under the residence-based taxation system; the company is subject to corporate income tax on net profits, and shareholders are not taxed through the entity (no full pass-through); the entity is within the South African 'company' definition under section 1 of the Income Tax Act and is not eligible for US-style pass-through classification; territorial scope applies only to non-resident companies with a South African permanent establishment, which is not the default for this locally incorporated entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under South African law. The available statutory elections for a resident (Pty) Ltd engaged in inter-affiliate finance or trading structures include: headquarter company election under section 9I of the Income Tax Act (applicable only to resident companies which are 100% directly or indirectly held by foreign shareholders and complying with the 80% foreign-derived income and other ring-fencing requirements); hybrid equity instrument treatment elections under section 8EA; CFC participation exemption election under section 9D(9) and section 9D(4); foreign exchange functional currency election under section 25D read with the Sixth Schedule; and the section 23A hybrid debt/equity designation rules affecting interest deductibility on funding instruments issued by the entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary VAT registration: ZAR 50,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period. A foreign person supplying taxable services in South Africa without a local fixed establishment must also register if such supplies exceed the compulsory threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS mandates electronic submission of VAT201 returns and supporting data through the eFiling platform with XML/API-based clearance interfaces; the National e-Invoice (NEI) Framework is being progressively phased in from 2024 for larger taxpayers, requiring near-real-time digital clearance of tax invoices to the SARS central system with cryptographic signature and SARS stamping for qualifying vendors; full audit-trail data reporting is required under the SARS 'data-as-a-utility' initiative, and all tax invoices must in any event comply with the substantive requirements of section 20 of the VAT Act, including the vendor's VAT number, sequential numbering, issue date, description of goods/services, consideration, and details of the recipient. Algorithmic high-frequency trading platforms must therefore maintain machine-readable invoice and transaction logs compatible with SARS API submission standards and real-time fiscal clearance protocols where mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the exporter is the vendor and the goods are physically removed from South Africa within 90 days of the time of supply; services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under section 11(2)(k) where the non-resident is not present in South Africa at the time the services are rendered and the services are not directly connected with land in South Africa or movable property situated in South Africa, and section 11(2)(l) zero-rates services physically rendered outside South Africa. For algorithmic market-making and proprietary HFT services, careful characterisation is essential: financial services rendered under section 2 of the VAT Act are generally exempt rather than zero-rated; however, a separately identifiable supply of trading, clearing, or data services to a non-resident counterparty that is not employed for the benefit of any South African business and is paid for in foreign currency may qualify for zero-rating where all statutory conditions and evidential requirements of section 11(2)(k)/(l) are satisfied. The zero-rating of exported services does not apply where the consideration is received from a South African resident or from a non-resident connected person in circumstances indicating a South African economic nexus.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of goods
Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or equivalent proof of foreign-currency payment
Packing List and Certificate of Origin where applicable
Vendor export evidential record retained under section 11(1) and section 55 of the VAT Act
Proof of settlement and trade execution logs for exported financial services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS applies heightened audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims, particularly where currency conversion and transaction timestamp anomalies suggest round-tripping. The burden of proof rests on the vendor to retain full documentary evidence for at least five years. Where a zero-rating claim is unsupported, SARS retrospectively claws back the output VAT at 15% on the deemed taxable supply, with interest from the original due date under section 187 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, and may impose an understatement penalty under sections 210-217 of the TAA of up to 200% of the shortfall where the claim is made negligently or with intentional disregard. In the case of fraudulent or deliberately falsified export documentation, section 60 of the VAT Act permits additional tax equal to 200% of the tax evaded; criminal prosecution also lies under section 72 of the VAT Act and section 234 of the TAA with imprisonment up to 10 years. In addition, SARS may set the clawed-back amounts off against any current refunds and publish the vendor as a non-compliant taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting specifically through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 (R.1111), and the National Payment System Act, 1998 (Act 78 of 1998). All commercial banks must hold Authorised Dealer status granted by FinSurv to execute foreign exchange transactions for residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is fully convertible on current account transactions (trade in services, dividends, interest, management fees) without prior FinSurv approval, provided the underlying transaction is bona fide and documented. Capital account transactions (inbound equity or loan capital, outward direct investment, offshore trading book funding) are liberalised but subject to registration and reporting requirements; non-resident shareholders may freely remit profits via the Authorised Dealer on presentation of audited financial statements, tax clearance (Form TCC from SARS), and a resolution of directors. For a proprietary algorithmic HFT entity, offshore trading balances constitute an 'offshore investment' and require prior approval per Exchange Control Regulation 9 unless executed through a SARB-approved asset management exemption; therefore the practical gateway is an Authorised Dealer-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) backed by a FinSurv-approved mandate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Regulation 6 of the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 and the Currency and Exchanges Manual (Rule 6.2) require all foreign currency export proceeds, including receipts for financial services and proprietary trading income attributable to a South African resident, to be repatriated to South Africa within 180 days of the date of entitlement. The full amount must be sold to an Authorised Dealer unless the exporter obtains a Foreign Currency Retention Account facility (permitted up to 100% of eligible proceeds) or a specific FinSurv exemption; for algorithmic market-making income, the 180-day surrender clock runs from the settlement date of the underlying trade, and any conversion into ZAR must be executed through the nominated Authorised Dealer with the appropriate BI-Form reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW for primary clearing and settlement; MEDIUM for ancillary low-value disbursements. Legal constraint: no offshore EMI or digital bank can clear ZAR directly or act as an Authorised Dealer in foreign exchange without a South African banking licence under the Banks Act, 1994, and FICA registration as an accountable institution. Global digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise Business, Payoneer, WorldFirst) may open segregated client accounts only via a partnered ZA Authorised Dealer; they cannot hold regulatory capital, provide local clearing house access, or issue ZAR payments through SAMOS. Additionally, FinSurv will not recognise an offshore EMI as the 'Authorised Dealer' for Exchange Control Regulation 9(2) reporting, meaning the HFT entity must maintain its primary foreign currency account at a licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA-accredited banks generally require the physical presence of at least two directors and the real-natured beneficial owner(s) for companies classified as Category II or III risk; however, since October 2021, SARB and the Financial Intelligence Centre permit risk-based remote onboarding using a notarised certified identity document and interactive biometric verification under FICA R.21(6). For algorithmic trading entities, most Tier 1 banks will still mandate a one-time in-person board interview at the Johannesburg or Cape Town corporate banking office because Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) cannot be fully discharged remotely where source-of-wealth complexity and rapid fund flows exist; a compliant alternative is a pre-approved remote electronic KYC session conducted via a qualified attorney or registered auditor acting as a verification agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding combined with fully automated high-frequency, sub-millisecond order execution creates a 'no-man-in-the-loop' AML narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute a Risk and Compliance Addendum describing the HFT algorithms (latency, order-to-trade ratio, venue connectivity, kill-switch logic); provide the FICA Data Retention Policy; submit the ISDA/JSE/CME participant agreements; furnish a certified true copy of the FIC registration certificate; and present a completed Transaction Monitoring Rationale explaining false-positive suppression.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border private fund flows where (Pty) Ltd is funded by foreign investors or offshore carried-interest payments are deemed to carry potential money-laundering or sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide investor onboarding files, subscription agreements, audited NAV reports, FATCA/CRS self-certifications, SARB Form F (foreign investment) approval letters, and a month-end reconciliation of Beneficiary vs Settlement balances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uncleared derivative margin and collateral transfers to foreign clearing houses may be perceived as disguised capital flight under Exchange Control Regulation 9.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the FinSurv offshore investment approval letter, executed ISDA/CSA and clearing membership agreements, daily initial/variation margin call statements, tri-party collateral schedules, and an audited list of all off-shore bank accounts and custody accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where the ultimate human owners are held through offshore trusts or nominees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Beneficial Ownership Register extract, full trust deed or foundation documents, a sworn affidavit of ultimate beneficial owner(s), and the SARS Tax Clearance Certificate proving tax residence status of every controlling party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin capitalisation and aggressive intra-group funding from related foreign treasury entities flag tax and exchange-control abuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File intercompany loan agreements, SARB loan registration confirmations, SARS transfer-pricing documentation (OECD TP template), an audited debt-to-equity ratio analysis, and the yearly tax-compliant interest payment schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed through a nominated Authorised Dealer (Tier 1 commercial bank) using SWIFT MT103 with the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) of ZA_PTY_LTD and a compliant beneficiary account format. For share capital, remitters must quote SARB purpose descriptor 'T' (foreign direct investment) or 'L' (loan) and complete the Inward Transfer Notification BI-Form; the bank will credit the ZAR Operational Account after automatic conversion or credit the FCA if the mandate permits retention. For USD Fedwire inbound transfers from foreign seed investors, the receiving ZA bank routes through its New York correspondent (typically The Standard Bank of South Africa NY branch) with intermediary bank BIC confirmation; the bank then posts to the ledger only upon receipt of (a) a company resolution, (b) the SARS Imported Capital Declaration, and (c) CIPC share allotment documentation to prove non-resident ownership.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for algorithmic market-making cover (i) clearing house margin calls, (ii) broker commissions, (iii) counterparty option premia, and (iv) trade settlement balances. The compliant rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 for low-value trade disbursements and third-party settlement via an Authorised Dealer using SARB Form C (Application for Foreign Payment); (b) MT202 COV for high-value clearing house settlements to JSE Clear, LCH, or CME via the bank's nostro account; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) where the HFT entity finances a physical commodity collateral basket; and (d) Direct Exchange Clearing for ZAR on SAMOS where same-day ZAR leg settlement occurs through the SARB settlement system. Each outbound payment requires an underlying transaction audit trail (trade tickets, exchange confirmations, broker statements) and must match the FinSurv-approved offshore mandate to avoid 'information mismatch' blocks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable ZAR/USD forward contracts (up to 12 months) executed through an Authorised Dealer, requiring evidence of the underlying offshore investment or receivable exposure.
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) used to roll over weekly margin funding without increasing net open position.
Cross-currency swaps (ZAR vs USD/EUR/GBP) for long-dated capital hedge of the proprietary trading book, subject to FinSurv approval beyond 12 months.
Vanilla and barrier FX options (calls/puts, knockout) with the same Authorised Dealer, provided the notional does not exceed five times the audited net asset value of the offshore book.

Deliverable ZAR non-delivery-excluded hedges are permitted; NDFs are NOT permissible because ZAR is a fully deliverable currency under the Currency and Exchanges Act, and any offshore NDF would be voided unless explicitly approved by FinSurv.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form CoR30.1) together with declaration regarding solvency, beneficial ownership confirmation and required filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each annual anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prescribed late-filing penalty accrues monthly for continued non-compliance; CIPC may issue a Notice of Final Deregistration and administratively strike off the company under Section 82 and Section 84 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 business days after any change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation is submitted together with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an offence under the Companies Act; monetary penalty or director disqualification can be imposed, and repeated failure may lead to administrative deregistration by CIPC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS), filed only when public interest score equals or exceeds 350 or when an FSCA licence condition mandates filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) where licence provisions require
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: With the Annual Return for CIPC purposes; not later than 4 months after financial year-end for FSCA-regulated licence conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under Section 34 of the Companies Act carrying a fine or imprisonment; administrative penalties and/or suspension of the financial-sector licence may be imposed by FSCA for repeated failure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for any company with a public interest score of 350 or more; for an FSCA-licensed algorithmic market-making entity, the licence condition typically imposes an independent annual audit irrespective of public interest score.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS as issued by the IASB, required for regulated financial-sector entities; IFRS for SMEs may be available to qualifying private companies but will not apply where the FSCA licence requires full IFRS financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Proprietary Limited company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office. Annual confirmation is embedded in the CIPC Annual Return and must be completed each anniversary. Any share transfer that alters beneficial ownership requires a CIPC BO-1 filing within 5 business days; intra-day proprietary trading positions do not by themselves create a filing event, only changes to the company's issued shareholding or ultimate controllers do.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (company tax rate per para (b) of the s5(1) rate schedule, applicable to years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; reduced from 28%)
